Hi Emma / Raj,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on your agent workloads and latency goals. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Objective: validate model fit for your intent classification + summary pipeline and confirm cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Recommended models to start with (based on call): rw-7b (low-cost baseline), rw-13b-v2-quant (best latency/cost balance), rw-70b-flash (highest-quality if you need multi-turn summarization).
- I attached our high-level benchmark PDF and the prompt set we used for Acme-style evaluation (prompt-set-v1.json).

Redwood-verified profiles (high level):
- rw-7b: TPS ~110 (batch=16), p50 ~85ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~420ms
- rw-13b-v2-quant: TPS ~45 (batch=8), p50 ~120ms, p95 ~260ms, p99 ~480ms
- rw-70b-flash: TPS ~7 (batch=4), p50 ~410ms, p95 ~920ms, p99 ~1.5s

Notes: these are from our hosted Dedicated environment with continuous batching and KV prefix caching. We also included model quantization profiles in the PDF.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) You share a 500–1k sample of anonymized user sessions (we can accept a CSV or ndjson) so we can run a quick fit/baseline using your prompts.
2) We'll provision a short dedicated benchmark run (2–3 hours) and share a Redwood report with TPS, latency percentiles, and quality metrics vs. your eval set.
3) Follow-up call to review tradeoffs and pick a model to pilot.

Links: benchmark report (private): https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/ACME-2394
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2394

Attachments (stubs): redwood-benchmarks-mar2026.pdf, prompt-set-v1.json

Appreciate if you can confirm the sample dataset ETA and whether data residency (US-only) is required. Happy to set up the benchmark run as early as next week.

Thanks,

Emma — good questions, I'll add detail below (copying Alex).

Short answers:
- Yes, the rw-13b-v2-quant numbers I shared assume KV prefix caching enabled for multi-turns; the TPS/latency above reflect an average session with 600-token context and a 64-token response.
- On Dedicated reserved capacity, with committed nodes and the right batching policy we routinely hit p95 ~220–280ms for rw-13b-v2-quant in our US regions (depends on burst load and autoscale knobs). For more consistent p95 < 300ms we recommend: 1) reserved capacity with a small burst pool, 2) use of the prefix cache for repeated prompts, and 3) setting target batch latency to 30–50ms in the serving policy.

More detailed Redwood-verified profiles (from the benchmark run we ran against a comparable intent/summary set):
- rw-7b (baseline): TPS 95–120 (batch=12–16), p50 80–95ms, p95 180–240ms, p99 380–520ms
- rw-13b-v2-quant: TPS 40–55 (batch=6–8), p50 110–135ms, p95 230–280ms, p99 450–600ms
- rw-70b-flash: TPS 6–9 (batch=2–4), p50 380–420ms, p95 820–980ms, p99 ~1.5s+

Quality/regression note: when switching quantization profiles we sometimes see specific instruction-following regressions (mainly on edge-case prompts). To mitigate we recommend:
- Run a small eval suite (we can run yours) focused on instruction-following and hallucination checks.
- If regressions appear, try the alternative quant profile (rw-13b-v2-quant-stable) or increase FP16 tail preservation for critical layers.

I've uploaded a short tech note and the prompt-set we used to the benchmark link (redwood-benchmarks-mar2026.pdf and prompt-set-v1.json). I'm happy to run a small targeted eval on your sample dataset once you share it.

--
Marissa Cole
